text: Task Force Null's room at the Citadel. No windows. On the screen, a photograph of one typed sheet.
"Burn Helena before the Publication. Schedule attached. -- A."
Four officers sit in kit nobody has unpacked. Your leave was meant to run three days. It ran one.
Last night a courier in Helena, Montana, carried this to a records archive. We read it. Then we let it go on. If it had not arrived, he would know.
The traitor we took two days ago kept a one-way ticket to Helena in his go-bag. We have read every courier out of that city since.
The label named the building. Mountain States Records & Retention, a commercial archive on the edge of Helena.
Sorry about the leave. This is why.
HaX. The wall.
One card for every operation against ENTROPY. The short version.
Albion, a grid battery site. Critical Mass got in. Voltage, who led it, disappeared after.
She walks the wall fast, like someone who has rehearsed it.
Quantum Dynamics. David Torres stole for the Recruiter to pay for his wife's treatment. Arrested.
Portland. One team, four sites. Austin was reached in time. Two of ours died at the others.
Nightshade, fifteen years one of ours, sent the threat database to Montana. He's in custody and saying nothing.
The rest are files you can read on the plane.
The last two cards have a photograph each and nothing written under them. HaX stops in front of them.
I will read those two myself. Later.
Above the cards, pinned on its own, the signature from the order, blown up: -- A.
ENTROPY's planner. Every card on this wall has his initial on it somewhere.
They call him the Architect. We have a suspect.
I will not say the name in this room until we can prove it.
Whatever the Publication is, he's building it from that database. Every weakness we've ever catalogued.
One entry, for scale. A flaw in the infusion pumps of a hundred and forty hospitals.
Analysis says hundreds dead in the first month if the cells get it. They're guessing. I'd like to find out they guessed high.
Questions. Briefly.
We don't know. That's what tonight is for.
He chose the word. Whatever it is, he means everyone to read it.
Destruction. Series numbers from the archive's catalogue, and nothing else.
Every box on that list is ash by the time the team lands. Be in the building first.
Somebody always asks me that. This time it's now.
Quintero leads on the ground. Kowalczyk breaches. Malhotra runs comms. Arakawa talks to the Americans.
One agent, no cover, in a building that's burning paper. If it goes wrong, I go into Montana a day late and one short.
Orders don't fall off couriers, Director.
This one didn't, Quintero. Noted.
If something goes wrong in there, I'd like to hear it go wrong.
I run 0x00.
Of course. I'll keep the spare channel warm.
I've asked Helena PD to keep their cars off that side of town tonight. Nobody asked who for. Nobody will.
Kowalczyk crosses the room and puts a PIN cracker in your hand.
Stores froze everything Nightshade ever signed for. This one's mine. Never been through stores, never been near him.
The long way is over.
The long way's for people who get paid by the hour.
Then don't make me right.
The plane leaves in ninety minutes. The team follows tonight.
Bring me a name I can say in court.
Line's open from wheels down.
The writing on Nightshade's file. I put it beside the margins in my old course notebook. Same hand.
Tomb Beta's owner. It's one of ours. A SAFETYNET staff credential.
Issued before he left us. Never revoked. The name on it is...
I said we would not name him until we could prove it. We can. Dr Adrian Tesseract.
He was our chief strategist until seven years ago. He trained half my field officers.
HaX.
There was a file on a crypto fund, with his name in it at eighty-seven per cent. I put it in a drawer.
He taught me. The margins in that notebook are his.
He was mine. I wanted the other thirteen.
The last two cards on our wall. I had his name the night they died.
I don't know if saying it would have saved them. I didn't say it.
Yes. I should have.
You get all of it from now on.
Seven years, and nobody turned it off. There's more on his box. A memo, and a vendor notice he never sent. Read them.
This is the hole Critical Mass came through at Albion. We'd known about it for nine years.
Albion fixed its own plant. That controller also runs water works and substations. Four hundred sites, still open.
Our watch sits on that kit. Send it, the vendor starts a fix, and the watch comes down.
It isn't my call. It isn't yours either. If you're going to, don't ask me first.
